"Multiple monitors This will help you can see all the information you need at once. Great for tasks that require a browser, email and spreadsheet at the same time! Beware having too many apps open though and it can become overwhelming."

"Emails Possibly the most distracting thing ever. Consider setting up rules so CCd emails go into a separate CC folder Company-wide emails can be filtered too Keep your inbox "clean" and if that doesn't work agree set times to review emails (such as first thing, 10am, 2pm, etc)"
"Prioritising Review your task list regularly and if you're unsure, engage your manager to review what needs to be done and which tasks are the most important. Set a top 5 and work from there."

"Deadlines!! If I'm asked to do something but not by a specific day/time it often doesn't get done... So ensure you either ask for a hard deadline, or encourage people to set one when requesting the work."

"Regular Breaks Working from home you can easily pop off for 5 mins to visit the kitchen for a brew or pop into the garden .. In the office, you may want to go for a walk around the building... Regular breaks help to give your brain a break and keep you focussed in the long-run."

"Written Instructions It is reasonable to request tasks are provided on email/written down. You may also need to make your own notes and review these together at the end of a discussion to ensure you have everything you need."

"Noise Cancelling Headphones This might not be viable for every job... If you work in an open plan office, see if you can wear your ANC headphones for work.  If you work in a call centre, your employer may be able to provide you with this so you can hear better on your calls."
